issues.legal_issue: Acceptance of a police final report does not bar a magistrate from taking cognizance on a further report arising from further investigation that uncovers fresh material.
material_facts: A complaint alleging criminal conduct was referred for police investigation, and the police submitted a final report stating that the complaint was false.
The magistrate accepted the final report, after which further investigation was ordered and fresh material came to light.
The police filed a further report alleging offences, and the magistrate took cognizance on that report.
The High Court quashed the cognizance order on the ground that acceptance of the first report deprived the magistrate of jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in quashing the cognizance order. The appeal was allowed, and the order setting aside cognizance was reversed; the respondents remained free to argue before the magistrate that no case was made out.
issues.legal_principle: Section 173(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 permits further investigation after a report under Section 173(2) has been submitted and contemplates forwarding a further report to the magistrate. A magistrate may take cognizance on that report if satisfied that an offence is disclosed. Under Pramatha Nath Taluqdar v. Saro Ranjan Sarkar, dismissal of a complaint under Section 203 does not absolutely bar a second complaint on the same facts; exceptional circumstances include the emergence of fresh evidence. The Court treated the fresh material here as supporting cognizance on the further police report, rather than as an impermissible second complaint. Bindeshwari Prasad Singh v. Kali Singh concerned a magistrate’s power to recall or review an order and did not decide this issue.

rule.if: police_cognizance_proceeding and earlier_final_report_accepted and further_investigation_conducted and fresh_material_discovered and further_report_indicates_offence

predicates.police_cognizance_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding in which a magistrate is asked to take cognizance on a police report.
predicates.earlier_final_report_accepted: A magistrate accepted an earlier police report that did not recommend prosecution.
predicates.further_investigation_conducted: Police conducted further investigation after submitting the earlier report.
predicates.fresh_material_discovered: The further investigation uncovered material not available when the earlier report was submitted.
predicates.further_report_indicates_offence: Police submitted a further report stating that an offence had been committed.

issues.definition: When a police cognizance proceeding follows an accepted final report, and further investigation uncovers fresh material that is presented in a report indicating an offence, the magistrate may take cognizance on that further report.
